newsitem.title: INDIA: India needs to invest 2.7 bln rupees in air cargo.
newsitem.headline: India needs to invest 2.7 bln rupees in air cargo.

text.p: India needs to spend 2.7 billion rupees ($75 million) to improve air cargo handling facilities at its four main international airports during the next five years, an Airports Authority of India (AAI) senior official told Reuters on Tuesday.
By 2005 the four international airports, Bombay, Calcutta, New Delhi and Madras are expected to handle 660,000 tonnes of international cargo, compared to 412,807 tonnes in 1995.
Air cargo accounts for around 40 percent of India's total exports, in value terms.

The official said two recently cleared projects included Delhi airport's 500 million rupees export terminal (phase three) which will exclusively handle courier or express cargo from the former the Commonwealth of Independent States.
Bids for its construction are being called and the project should be ready within two years.
Another 10,000 square metres terminal in Delhi will handle imports.

The AAI is also considering private investment to set up a dedicated 5,000 sq. metre terminal for perishable goods in Bombay. The AAI will be the "custodian" of this terminal, which is expected to cost around 300 million rupees and enter operation within two years.

The official said there were also plans afoot for specialised courier terminals at Bombay, Delhi and Madras, and integrated cargo terminals in addition to then increase in existing capacity, at Bombay and Delhi.
Bombay's integrated terminal will be constructed in four phases, the first one will cost 400 million rupees. The site has been identified, but the government still has to settle privatisation terms.
The AAI is vetting similar proposals for Calcutta and Madras.
Calicut, Coimbatore, Hyderabad and Nagpur will be served by domestic cargo terminals, he said.
A comprehensive air freight 'city' is planned for Delhi.
Indian airports currently suffer a prolonged "dwell time" of over 21 days for imports and three days for exports.

Air cargo agents want procedures simplified, especially for exports. They want a single-window service for all cargo related queries, procedures and documentation, and a single document for clearance of imports. They have also suggested the introduction of an electronic data interchange system connecting all partners in international airports.
